subject: Clarify: model-improvement opt-out, prompt/response custody, subprocessors & escrow options
messages:
From: Sara Lee <sara.lee@medalign.health>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@medalign.health
Date: 2027-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Redwood DPA & AI usage — request for explicit model-improvement opt-out and custody terms

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the demo last week — we liked the latency profile and the dedicated routing options. Legal looped me in with a couple of asks we need resolved before procurement can move forward:

- Explicit commitment that MedAlign data will not be used to improve models (training or continuous fine-tuning) without our prior written consent.
- Clear language that prompts we send and the responses generated by the model are considered customer content and that MedAlign retains ownership/custody — we need to avoid ambiguous derivative claims.
- A current list of subprocessors and the ability to require onshore processing for any PHI-derived interactions.
- Operational options if we need verifiable evidence for the no-improvement commitment (audit logs, export, or escrow).

Can you point me to the clause set you typically offer and any evidence pack or operational runbook that your ops team can provide? Procurement is sensitive to anything that suggests our data could be used to train open models.

Appreciate a quick confirmation of next steps and timelines.

Best,
Sara
Head of Privacy, MedAlign Health

[Attachment: MedAlign_request_summary.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lee <sara.lee@medalign.health>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-02T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA & AI usage — request for explicit model-improvement opt-out and custody terms

Hi Sara — thanks, and glad the demo went well. Looping in Jordan (product) and David (privacy/legal) so we can give you a consolidated response and an operational path. Initial answers below; attaching our suggested redlines and an ops runbook draft.

Short answers up front:
- We can commit to a Customer-Directed "no-model-improvement" setting per account: we will mark MedAlign interactions as opt-out at ingestion and ensure they are excluded from all training pipelines and model updates. We call this the "model-improvement opt-out".
- Prompt and response custody: we propose explicit DPA language that treats submitted prompts and generated outputs as "Customer Content", granting MedAlign ownership of that content and exclusive rights to derivative works created by MedAlign.
- Subprocessors: attached is our current list. We support onshore routing for specific data classes (PHI) via a policy and KMS key scoping.
- Evidence: we can provide an evidence bundle (audit logs, per-request metadata, routing records) and an export path (SFTP or customer S3) for a defined time window. We can also offer a limited escrow option for outputs if required for contract closure.

Next steps we recommend:
1) Legal redlines: review attached "MedAlign_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf."
2) Ops sync: Jordan will propose an operational cutover plan for onshore routing and per-account opt-out enforcement.
3) Evidence pack: David will outline the evidence artifacts we can provide and expected lead time.

Jordan / David — can you confirm feasibility and runtime implications (cost/latency) for per-account opt-out + onshore routing? If feasible, we will draft the wording for the DPA addendum and a short operational SLA for evidence delivery.

Thanks — Evelyn
Head of Product & Ops, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: MedAlign_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: operational-runbook-no-train.md (markdown)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Sara Lee <sara.lee@medalign.health>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-05T14:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA & AI usage — request for explicit model-improvement opt-out and custody terms

Hi all — quick technical note on feasibility and expected operational behavior if MedAlign requires the opt-out + onshore processing:

- Model-improvement opt-out: We can implement at ingestion a per-tenant flag that tags records as "no-improve". Those records are omitted from all training/finetune data exports and filtered from any internal sampling pipelines. This is implemented in the runtime (inference gateway) so it's enforced server-side.
- Prompt/Response custody: We maintain ephemeral KV cache for generation; by default we retain minimal telemetry. For customers that demand custody rights we can:
  * Store full request/response pairs in a customer-dedicated, encrypted bucket (tenant-scoped) for export on request.
  * Provide a signed export manifest (hashes + timestamps) so MedAlign can verify completeness of an export.
- Onshore routing: We can route requests to onshore pools when a PHI marker is present. This requires a customer KMS key (for onshore encryption at rest) and a short config window to pin routing policy.
- Evidence/escrow: Options we can offer:
  1) Scheduled SFTP export of request/response artifacts for a rolling 30/90 day window.
  2) One-off export on audit request (sealed manifest + GPG signature).
  3) Escrow of generated outputs (customer-provided or Redwood-hosted vault) for a limited term under escrow agreement — this has legal/ops overhead but is doable.

Tradeoffs: onshore routing increases tail latency by ~15–40ms depending on pool; dedicated storage/export increases storage and transfer costs (we'll provide an estimate).

I'll draft an "Operational Runbook — MedAlign" that details the API knobs, expected latency and cost delta, and the export manifest format.

-Jordan
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lee <sara.lee@medalign.health>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-09T11:29:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA & AI usage — request for explicit model-improvement opt-out and custody terms

Sara — following up on the legal side. A few items for clarity so our DPA redlines align with MedAlign procurement needs:

1) Scope of "no-improvement": please confirm whether this needs to apply to both "raw interaction text" and any derived telemetry (e.g., anonymized embeddings, logs). We typically exclude raw interactions, but some customers also require the exclusion of derived artifacts — we can accommodate but need to enumerate which artifacts.

2) Verification cadence: do you require on-demand audit exports (per incident) or periodic attestations (quarterly)? Per-request exports are operationally heavier and may require an addendum to SOW.

3) Escrow: we can offer generated-output escrow, but typical escrow workflows require a mutually agreed escrow agent and clear destruction/return timelines. If MedAlign wants escrowed copies of prompts & responses, we'll need to scope retention windows and access controls.

4) Subprocessor gating: we can add a clause allowing MedAlign to require onshore processing for a subset of data categories. We will provide our full subprocessor list and an amendment workflow for adding/removing subprocessors with 30-day notification.

Attached is a short checklist that helps us pin definitions (what counts as "derived" vs "raw"). If you can mark the items and return, we will convert into DPA language and a procurement SOW with the ops costs.

Thanks — David
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: no-improve-scope-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Sara Lee <sara.lee@medalign.health>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@medalign.health
Date: 2027-12-12T16:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA & AI usage — request for explicit model-improvement opt-out and custody terms

Evelyn / David — thanks for the clear plan and attachments. We reviewed the redlines and runbook draft. A few confirmations from our side:

- Scope: the opt-out must cover raw interaction text plus embeddings that could be used to recreate or cluster our data. We will mark those as "sensitive-derived" on the checklist.
- Verification: we will take quarterly attestations during the first 12 months and reserve the right to request one on-demand export with 30 days' notice in case of an audit.
- Escrow: we prefer the escrow option for generated outputs for the initial pilot. Please propose an escrow agent and a retention/return schedule.
- Subprocessors: please send the subprocessor list and the amendment workflow (30-day notice is fine).

If you can incorporate these into the DPA addendum and send a DocuSign for a pilot SOW, procurement will fast-track.

Sara
Head of Privacy, MedAlign Health
